messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed a sudden spike of GPU evictions and network errors in ord3. Peering looks flaky from our edge metrics.

devin: seeing it too. eviction rate ~30% on gpu-pool-ord3 over past 6m. p95 latency for hosted API jumped to 1.8s :grimacing:

ashok: provider status shows a peering degradation affecting a subset of interconnects in ORD3. opened case with them.

jess: hosted request timeouts are causing retries and extra load. Can we shift traffic off ord3 to ord1/eu-west while they investigate? @devin

devin: I’ll start gradual reroute. plan: route override to move 20%->50% traffic to ord1, keep 50% in ord3 initially: `routemgr set-priority ord1 0.2 && routemgr set-priority ord3 0.8`

sre-bot: Alert fired: GPU_EVICTIONS_HIGH for ord3. Runbook triggered: regional-eviction-incident. Link: https://redwood.inc/runbooks/regional-eviction-incident

ashok: digging into node logs — looks like NIC resets right before eviction. snippet:

[ 1234.567890] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: NIC port 1 link down
[ 1234.572100] gpu_vm(0): eviction initiated: host network unreachable

maria: NIC flaps -> can't rely on steady KV/cache traffic. Recommend draining non-critical low-priority workloads and shifting any high throughput canaries off ord3.

devin: draining low-prio nodes now: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-a -l pool=ord3-lowpri && kubectl drain gpu-node-a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (rolling across nodes)

jess: draining started. moving ~40% of dedicated reserved capacity to ord1 as temporary fallback. this will increase hourly spend, pinging finance.

iris: provider says KMS/HSM unaffected, so no key failures. CDN peering is degraded — client requests falling back to longer paths, which causes retries and amplifies load to ord3.

ashok: provider case CASE-78291: they recommend traffic engineering on our prefixes at the peering edge. implemented AS-path prepending on the affected prefixes as a mitigation.

devin: applied prepends, watching p99 & packet loss. early signal: p99 decreased ~10%, packet loss down from 3.5% to 2.1% on affected links.

maria: pause any new canary rollouts to ord3. @deploy-bot pause
deploy-bot: Canary rollouts paused by maria (requested at 1792003600).

jess: notifying top 10 customers on dedicated about degraded ord3 capacity and temporary fallback to ord1. email draft shared in #customer-success.

iris: finance confirmed temporary overage allowance for availability window. we should still optimize to reduce bill where possible.

devin: next steps: keep drains active, keep AS prepends for 2h, re-evaluate eviction rate. if evictions <5% and p95 stable, incrementally shift traffic back. if not, initiate warm-up of ord1 cold-standby and schedule cross-region redistrib.

maria: thanks — update the incident doc with timeline and attach NIC dumps for provider. link incident: https://redwood.inc/ops/incidents/1792003456. follow-up: post-mortem and cost reconciliation tomorrow.
